chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Saffan, from al-Hariz, from al-Bukayr, from one of the Imams (peace be upon him), that he said:
Whoever accuses a Muslim of zina (or false testimony), he is to be given eighty stripes, whether he is a Jew, a Christian, or a slave.

key_terms.مَنِ افْتَرَى: He who accuses (specifically of zina or qadhf)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for falsely accusing a Muslim of adultery in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies that the standard hadd punishment of eighty lashes for qadhf applies uniformly to the accuser, irrespective of whether they are a Jew, Christian, or a slave, emphasizing the egalitarian nature of this specific penal code. It highlights the juristic consensus that social hierarchy or religious difference does not mitigate the penalty for falsely accusing a Muslim of zina. This ruling is particularly significant in Shia fiqh for establishing the consistency of legal retribution across different social strata.
